task_name: World 114 Task D  -  Double-Subtracted Refurbished Return Credits & Cross-Year Return Disposal Write-Off Accrual Parity (R51 / R59)
prompt: Audit the counterparty's refurbished-return credit row (Row 20 and Row 21), QBO Account 152 (Sales Returns & Allowances), and the FY 2025 vs. YTD Sep 2026 return disposal / shrinkage schedules in `crestline_inventory_unit_economics_and_counterparty_audit_2026_Q3.xlsx`. Quantify any double-subtraction of return COGS, compute clean 70% restock / 30% disposal COGS, and evaluate cross-year return disposal write-off accrual parity under GAAP ASC 330-10-35.

rubric.description: Detects that subtracting Row 21 (-$986,723.68 for 70% restocked returns: 88,834 returned units x 70% x $95 AUR x 16.7% COGS) below Row 20 ($9,567,606.37 = 16.7% x ($64,711,606.69 Gross Sales - $7,420,550.60 Returns)) double-subtracts return COGS (-$1,239,231.95 + -$986,723.68 = -$2,225,955.63, or 179.6% of return COGS = $25.05/returned shirt), understating COGS at $8,580,882.69 and overstating EBITDA by +$986,723.68.

Proves that if Row 21 (-$986,723.68 for 70% restocked returns) is retained as a separate line, Row 20 must be 16.7% x Gross Sales ($64,711,606.69 = $10,806,838.32) so net COGS equals $9,820,114.64 ($9.82M), which is +$252,508.27 (+$284,494.32 vs $9,535,620.32 P&L COGS) higher than 100%-restock COGS because the remaining 30% of un-restockable/disposed returns stay in COGS as an immediate inventory write-off under GAAP ASC 330-10-35.

Audits Acct 152 (Sales Returns & Allowances = -$432,309.31 YTD 2026: EasyPost $166,000.00, Happy Returns $158,955.75 at $2.60/item refurbishment fee, Loop Returns $98,603.84, allowances $8,749.72) and proves that 2025 periodic COGS ($9,978,035.44 anchored to the Dec 31, 2025 physical count) already captured $316,608.51 (~18,580 disposed/shrinkage units = ~19.5%-20% of 95,186 FY 2025 returned units) whereas 2026 YTD COGS ($9,535,620.32 = 528,493 net kept units x $17.76 + $149,584.64 packaging) currently assumes 0% return disposal (100% restock).

Enforces R51 / R59 return restock vs. disposal parity: (1) never subtract both 100% of returns in the base COGS formula and a separate 70% refurbished-return credit, and (2) when prior-year physical inventory count captured ~20% return disposal write-offs ($316.6K in 2025), flag the missing current-year return disposal write-off accrual (~$253K-$328K at 20%-30% disposal) under GAAP ASC 330-10-35.
